chunks: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) wrote to Sa'd al-Khayr: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. To proceed: I counsel you to taqwa (God-consciousness) of God, for in it lies safety from destruction and gain upon the return. God, Mighty and Majestic, protects the servant through taqwa from that which his intellect has lost sight of, and through taqwa He clears away his blindness and ignorance. And it was through taqwa that Noah and those with him in the ark were saved, and Salih and those with him from the thunderbolt.

And through taqwa the patient ones triumphed and those groups were saved from destructions. They have brothers on that path seeking that virtue — they have abandoned their transgression in indulging desires upon hearing of the punishments in the Book. They praised their Lord for what He has sustained them, and He is worthy of praise; and they censured themselves for what they fell short of, and they are worthy of censure. They knew that God, Blessed and Exalted, the Forbearing, the All-Knowing — His wrath is only upon whoever does not accept His pleasure from Him, and He only withholds from whoever does not accept His gift from Him, and He only leads astray whoever does not accept His guidance from Him. Then He enabled the people of sins to repent by replacing (sins) with good deeds. He called His servants in the Book to that with a voice that did not cease, and He did not prevent the supplication of His servants. So God cursed those who conceal what God has revealed, and He prescribed upon Himself mercy, so it preceded His wrath and was completed in truth and justice — He does not begin with wrath toward servants before they provoke His anger. And that is from the knowledge of certainty and the knowledge of taqwa. Every community from which God has lifted the knowledge of the Book — that is when they abandoned it; and He subjected them to their enemy when they took him as master.

And it was part of their rejection of the Book that they preserved its letters while distorting its limits. So they recite it but do not observe it. The ignorant are impressed by their memorization of narrations, while the scholars are grieved by their abandonment of observance. And it was part of their rejection of the Book that they entrusted it to those who do not know, who led them into caprice and drove them to ruin, and they altered the bonds of religion; then they bequeathed it in foolishness and youth. So the community follows the command of people after the command of God, Blessed and Exalted, and to it they are returned. How evil a substitute for the wrongdoers: the guardianship of people after the guardianship of God, the reward of people after the reward of God, and the pleasure of people after the pleasure of God. So the community came to be in that state, and among them were those who strive in worship upon that very misguidance — self-impressed, beguiled. So their worship became a trial for them and for those who followed them. Indeed, in the messengers there was a reminder for those who worship. There was a prophet among the prophets who would perfect obedience, then would disobey God, Blessed and Exalted, in a single matter, and thereby he was expelled from Paradise and cast into the belly of the whale. Then nothing saved him except acknowledgment and repentance.

So recognize the counterparts of the clergy and monks who went along with concealing the Book and distorting it — their commerce did not profit them and they were not guided. Then recognize their counterparts in this community — those who preserved the letters of the Book but distorted its limits. They are with the masters and the elite, and when the leaders of caprice diverge, they side with whichever has more worldly wealth; that is the extent of their knowledge. They remain in that state — in worldly disposition and greed — and the voice of Iblis is ever heard upon their tongues with much falsehood. The scholars among them endure harm and insults, while they find fault with the scholars for placing demands. Yet the scholars are themselves guilty of treachery if they conceal sincere counsel: if they see one lost and astray, they do not guide him; or one spiritually dead, they do not revive him. How evil is what they do! For God, Blessed and Exalted, took from them a covenant in the Book: to command good and what they were commanded, to forbid what they were forbidden, to cooperate in righteousness and piety, and not to cooperate in sin and transgression. So the scholars struggle against the ignorant in effort and striving: if they exhort them, they say 'they have rebelled'; if they teach the truth that they abandoned, they say 'they have opposed'; if they withdraw from them, they say 'they have separated'; if they say 'bring your proof for what you claim,' they say 'they have acted hypocritically'; and if they obey them, they say 'they have disobeyed God, Mighty and Majestic.'

So the ignorant perish in what they do not know — illiterate regarding what they recite — accepting the Book when it is presented clearly, but rejecting it when it is distorted; and they do not object. Those are the counterparts of the clergy and monks: leaders in caprice, masters in ruin. And others among them sit between misguidance and guidance — they cannot distinguish one group from the other. They say: 'The people did not know this and did not understand what it was.' They have vindicated it: the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, left them on a pure white path whose night is like its day — no innovation appeared among them and no Sunnah was changed; no disagreement among them and no difference. But when the darkness of their sins overcame people, they became two Imams: one calling to God, Blessed and Exalted, and one calling to the Fire. At that point Satan spoke and his voice rose upon the tongues of his allies, and his cavalry and infantry multiplied, and he shared in the wealth and children of those who associated him; so innovation was practiced and the Book and Sunnah were abandoned. And the allies of God spoke with proof and held fast to the Book and wisdom.

From that day onward, the people of truth and the people of falsehood became divided. The people of guidance faltered and made peace with one another, while the people of misguidance cooperated, until the assembly was with so-and-so and his ilk. Know this type, and there is another type — see them with your own eyes among the noble ones, and keep close to them until you return to your family. For the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Is it not so that this is the manifest loss? [Up to here is the narration of al-Husayn, and in the narration of Muhammad ibn Yahya there is an addition:] They have knowledge of the path — if there is affliction in their way, do not look to them for guidance; and if there is oppression from the people of oppression, and hardship, and before them are trials that will pass and then turn to ease — then know that the trusted brothers are treasures for one another. Were it not that my suspicions might drive you away from me, I would have revealed to you certain truths I have concealed, and I would have disclosed to you certain truths I have kept hidden. But I act with taqwa toward you and preserve your safety. The truly forbearing person is not one who acts without wariness of anyone, in the place of taqwa. Forbearance is the garment of the learned — do not ever be stripped of it. And peace.

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْبَاطِل: The people of falsehood — those who follow innovation and worldly authority
key_terms.أَهْلُ الْحَقِّ: The people of truth — those who follow the Quran and the Imams
key_terms.التَّقْوَى: Taqwa — God-consciousness, piety, the shield against ruin
key_terms.الْبِدْعَة: Innovation (bid'a) — introduction of new practices into religion contrary to the sunnah
key_terms.الْحُجَّة: The Proof — the authoritative argument; also title of the Imam as God's proof on earth
key_terms.الْحُدُود: The limits/boundaries — the practical rulings and injunctions of the Quran
key_terms.الْحِلْم: Forbearance/clemency — the mark of true scholarship and leadership
key_terms.الْكِتَاب: The Book — the Quran, whose letters were preserved but limits distorted
key_terms.الْمِيثَاق: The covenant — the obligation taken from scholars in the Quran to enjoin good and forbid evil
key_terms.وَلَايَةُ اللَّهِ: The guardianship/authority of God — the divine wilaya transmitted through the Imams

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir write to Sa'd al-Khayr about taqwa and the corruption of religion?
ai.summary: This is a letter from Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (peace be upon him), the fifth Imam of the Shia, to his companion Sa'd al-Khayr, written as a comprehensive ethical and theological treatise. The letter counsels taqwa (God-consciousness) as the foundation of all virtue, then expounds on the corruption of religion by those who preserve the outward forms of the Book while distorting its living boundaries, contrasting the people of falsehood — who follow desire and worldly authority — with the people of truth who cling to the Quran and the Imams. The letter was written in a context of religious confusion after the Prophet's passing, when the community had split between those who followed true guidance and those who followed innovation, and Sa'd al-Khayr, a trusted companion, needed both spiritual instruction and guidance for navigating the treacherous religious and political landscape.
